The registers $V_I$ and $V_X$ are disjoint, so the second level is supported on a register subspace disjoint from the first, and summing the two contributions gives $\\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\\, s,\\, 0\\bigr)$, which is $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v)$ by Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-alnf}.\n    73\t\\end{proof}\n    74\t\n    75\t\\begin{lemma}[Level of the diagonal line map]\\label{lem:ld-dline-level}\n    76\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinear_ldDLineCL}\n    77\t\t\\leanok\n    78\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:cl-func}\n    79\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}. The map $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ of Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-dlnf} is a $3$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.\n    80\t\\end{lemma}\n    81\t\\begin{proof}\n    82\t\t\\leanok\n    83\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative}\n    84\t\tThe following data exhibit $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ as a $3$-level conditionally linear function. Its first level is the projection of $V$ onto the coordinate register $V_I$. For a first-level value with coordinate component $s$, its second level is the linear map $v \\mapsto \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ with $i = \\chi(s)$ on the direction register $V_V$. For a second-level value with direction component $v'$, its third level is the linear map $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ on the point register $V_X$. The registers $V_I$, $V_V$ and $V_X$ are pairwise disjoint, so each level is supported on a register subspace disjoint from the preceding ones, and summing the three contributions gives $\\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{\\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\\, s,\\, \\pi_{i-1}(v)\\bigr)$, which is $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v)$ by Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-dlnf}.\n    85\t\\end{proof}\n    86\t\n    87\t\\begin{lemma}[The low-degree question distribution is a typed CL distribution]\\label{lem:ld-question-typed-cl}\n    88\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL}\n    89\t\t% No completion mark: the linked declaration proves the distribution identity only, not the typed-family assertion. See the last paragraph of the statement; the open family assertion is tracked by issue 180.\n    90\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:typed-cl-distributions, def:graph-distribution, lem:ld-aline-level, lem:ld-dline-level}\n    91\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}, let $L = \\{L_t\\}_{t \\in \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}}$ be the family of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}, and let $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ be the graph on $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ all of whose unordered pairs, self-loops included, are edges. Then the question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is the $(\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}, G^{\\mathrm{ld}})$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\\mu^{G^{\\mathrm{ld}}}_{L,\\,L}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions}. The linked declaration proves the distribution identity: the question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ equals the distribution that the construction of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions} produces from the pair $(L, L)$ and the graph $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, a construction that is available for an arbitrary family of maps. It does not prove that $L$ is a $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$-typed family of conditionally linear functions of one common level, which is what makes the right-hand side a typed conditionally linear distribution in the sense of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions}: Lemmas~\\ref{lem:ld-aline-level} and~\\ref{lem:ld-dline-level} give the levels of $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ and $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$, while the level of $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$ and the passage of the three maps to a common level are not formalized. That family assertion is open and is tracked as issue~\\#180, so the statement and the proof below carry no completion mark.\n    92\t\\end{lemma}\n    93\t\\begin{proof}\n    94\t\t% No completion mark: the Lean proof establishes the distribution identity only; the typed-family hypotheses on L are open and tracked by issue 180.\n    95\t\t\\uses{def:typed-cl-distributions, def:graph-distribution, def:cl-dist}\n    96\t\tEvery unordered pair of types is an edge of $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, so the graph distribution $\\mu_{G^{\\mathrm{ld}}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:graph-distribution} is the uniform distribution on $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$. For each ordered type pair $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{t_{\\mathrm A}},\\, L_{t_{\\mathrm B}}}$ is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{t_{\\mathrm A}}(z), L_{t_{\\mathrm B}}(z)\\bigr)$. Binding the uniform type pair to these push-forwards and tagging each content with its type is exactly the two-stage sampling procedure of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}. This establishes the distribution identity; the typed-family hypotheses on $L$ are not established here.\n    97\t\\end{proof}\n    98\t\n    99\tThe next two lemmas show that the CL functions $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ give rise to the axis-parallel and diagonal line-versus-point distributions.\n   100\tWe label the coordinates by $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,m-1\\}$, with label $r$\n   101\trepresenting the paper's coordinate $r+1$.\n   102\t\n   103\t\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:alnf}\n   104\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_mem_line}\n   105\t\t\\leanok\n   106\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n   107\t\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, e_i)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a line that goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n   108\t\\end{lemma}\n   109\t\\begin{proof}\n   110\t\t\\leanok\n   111\t\t\\uses{def:cl-dist, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative, lem:line-rep-incidence}\n   112\t\tBy Definition~\\ref{def:cl-dist} the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(z), L_{\\mathsf{Point}}(z)\\bigr)$, so each marginal below is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along the composite of that map with the corresponding coordinate. The point marginal is the image of the uniform distribution on $V$ under $(u,s,v) \\mapsto u$, hence uniform on $\\F_q^m$. The axis marginal is its image under $(u,s,v) \\mapsto \\chi(s)$; since $m$ divides $q$, every fibre of $\\chi$ has exactly $q/m$ elements, so $i = \\chi(s)$ is uniform on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$ and $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$. Finally the base point recorded in the sample is $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u)$, which is fixed by $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}$ (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}) and satisfies $u \\in \\ell(u_0,e_i)$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:line-rep-incidence}.\n   113\t\\end{proof}\n   114\t\n   115\t\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:dlnf}\n   116\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_mem_line, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_prefix_zero}\n   117\t\t\\leanok\n   118\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n   119\t\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, v)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a random diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares its first $i-1$ coordinates with $u$, for uniformly random $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n   120\t\\end{lemma}\n   121\t\\begin{proof}\n   122\t\t\\leanok\n   123\t\t\\uses{def:cl-dist, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative, lem:line-rep-incidence}\n   124\t\tThe three steps are those of the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:alnf}, and none of them depends on that lemma. The two marginals are again push-forwards of the uniform distribution on $V$ along coordinates of $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(z), L_{\\mathsf{Point}}(z)\\bigr)$, by Definition~\\ref{def:cl-dist}: the point marginal is uniform on $\\F_q^m$, and $i = \\chi(s)$ is uniform on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$ because every fibre of $\\chi$ has $q/m$ elements. The direction component of the sampled tuple is $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$, whose first $i-1$ coordinates vanish and which is unchanged by a further application of $\\pi_{i-1}$. Finally $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}(u)$ is fixed by $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}) and satisfies $u \\in \\ell(u_0,v')$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:line-rep-incidence}.\n   125\t\\end{proof}\n   126\t\n   127\t\\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]\\label{def:line-point-dist}\n   128\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineKind, MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineDesc}\n   129\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist}\n   130\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist}\n   131\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_isProbability}\n   132\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_isProbability}\n   133\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_isProbability}\n   134\t\t\\leanok\n   135\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, lem:alnf, lem:dlnf}\n   136\t\tThe \\emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,e_i),\\, u)$, where we omit the $0$ components for simplicity. The \\emph{diagonal line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,s,v),\\, u)$. The \\emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{Line}}$ is the equal mixture of the two: with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, and with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$.\n   137\t\\end{definition}\n   138\t\n   139\t\\begin{definition}[Win predicate of the classical low individual degree game]\\label{def:ld-win-predicate}\n   140\t\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line, def:polyfunc}\n   141\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$. Answers in the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ take the following forms, depending on the question type; answers not of the prescribed form are rejected.\n   142\t\t\\begin{itemize}\n   143\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{Point}$, question content $u \\in \\F_q^m$: the answer is an element of $\\F_q^k$.\n   144\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{ALine}$, question content $(u_0,s) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q$, specifying the axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$ with $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple $(f_1,\\ldots,f_k)$ of univariate polynomials $f_j\\colon \\F_q \\to \\F_q$ of degree at most $d$, each given by its $d+1$ coefficients.\n   145\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{DLine}$, question content $(u_0,s,v) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q \\times \\F_q^m$, specifying the diagonal line $\\ell(u_0,v')$ with $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple of univariate polynomials of degree at most $md$.\n   146\t\t\\end{itemize}\n   147\t\tThe win predicate $D^{\\mathrm{ld}} = D^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the function of the tuple $(t_{\\mathrm A}, x_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B}, x_{\\mathrm B}, a_{\\mathrm A}, a_{\\mathrm B})$ determined by the following clauses, evaluated for $w \\in \\{\\mathrm A,\\mathrm B\\}$; in all cases where no action is indicated, the predicate accepts.\n   148\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   149\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Consistency test}) If $t_{\\mathrm A} = t_{\\mathrm B}$, accept if and only if $a_{\\mathrm A} = a_{\\mathrm B}$.\n   150\t\t\t% The source phrases both clauses with \"the\" t such that x = u_0 + tv; that phrase\n   151\t\t\t% does not determine t on diagonal questions with direction v' = 0, which the\n   152\t\t\t% question distribution samples with positive probability. The universal\n   153\t\t\t% quantification over t used here is the local correction; see the remark below.\n   154\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Axis-parallel line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \\mathsf{ALine}$ and $t_{\\overline w} = \\mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\\overline w})_j$ for all $j \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,k\\}$ and all $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t e_i$, where $i = \\chi(s)$.\n   155\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Diagonal line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \\mathsf{DLine}$ and $t_{\\overline w} = \\mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\\overline w})_j$ for all $j \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,k\\}$ and all $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$, where $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \\chi(s)$.\n   156\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   157\t\tThe game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the typed game with type set $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, the question distribution of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}, and win predicate $D^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$.\n   158\t\\end{definition}\n   159\t\n   160\t\\begin{remark}[Diagonal questions with zero direction]\\label{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}\n   161\t\tThe source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\\ell(u_0, 0) = \\{u_0\\}$, every $t \\in \\F_q$ satisfies $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \\mapsto u_0 + t \\cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}$.\n   162\t\\end{remark}\n   163\t\n   164\tThe soundness properties of the low individual degree game are expressed in terms of the following class of measurements.\n   165\t\n   166\t\\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]\\label{def:ld-meas}\n   167\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyIndex, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeas, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeasFamily, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeasTuple}\n   168\t\t\\leanok\n   169\t\t\\uses{def:polyfunc, def:polymeasurements, def:polynomials-degree}\n   170\t\tLet $\\polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ denote the set of POVM measurements indexed by $\\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, the polynomial representatives of individual degree at most $d$ in each variable; this is the notion of Definition~\\ref{def:polymeasurements}, and the argument order $(m,q,d)$ follows that definition (the paper orders the arguments as $(m,d,q)$). By Definition~\\ref{def:polynomials-degree}, evaluation identifies these representatives with the corresponding polynomial functions $g\\colon \\F_q^m \\to \\F_q$, bijectively whenever $d \\le q-1$; at the canonical parameters (Definition~\\ref{def:introparams}, where $d = 1 \\le q-1$) the identification is bijective; the general statements of this chapter quantify over all admissible tuples and are read through the representative convention. More generally, for an integer $k$ and tuples $m = (m_1,\\ldots,m_k)$, $q = (q_1,\\ldots,q_k)$, $d = (d_1,\\ldots,d_k)$, let $\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)$ denote the set of measurements $G = \\{G_{g_1,\\ldots,g_k}\\}$ such that for each $i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,k\\}$, the outcome index $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i\\colon \\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \\to \\F_{q_i}$ of individual degree at most $d_i$.\n   171\t\tThe tuple components are labelled by $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,k-1\\}$, with\n   172\t\tlabel $r$ representing the paper's component $r+1$.\n   173\t\\end{definition}\n   174\t\n   175\tQuantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \\emph{total} degree was claimed by Natarajan and Vidick, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test by Vidick; there is a known gap in the soundness analysis of that test, and it is not used here. Instead, the construction relies on the low \\emph{individual} degree test, whose quantum soundness is proved in~\\cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} and generalized in~\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}. The statement below is the form most directly useful in what follows.\n   176\t\n   177\t% The paper states this result in a theorem environment with the label lem:ld-soundness.\n   178\t% We keep both the environment and the label verbatim for cross-reference fidelity.\n   179\t\\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test]\\label{lem:ld-soundness}\n   180\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaLd, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness}\n   181\t\t\\leanok\n   182\t\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:projective-strategy-general, def:tensor-product-value, def:consistency, def:bracket}\n   183\t\tThere exists a function\n   184\t\t\\[\n   185\t\t\t\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}(\\eps, q, m, d, k) = a\\,(dmk)^a \\bigl(\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\\bigr)\n   186\t\t\\]\n   187\t\tfor universal constants $a \\ge 1$ and $0 < b \\le 1$ such that the following holds. For all $\\eps > 0$ and every parameter tuple $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game} (so $m, d, k \\ge 1$, $q$ is an admissible field size, and $m$ divides $q$), and for all projective strategies $(\\psi, A, B)$ that succeed with probability at least $1-\\eps$ in the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$, there exist measurements\n   188\t\t\\[\n   189\t\t\tG^w \\in \\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)\n   190\t\t\\]\n    30\t\n    31\t/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient\n    32\tspace uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a\n    33\tmodel supplied by each parameter record.  This is the Lean carrier for\n    34\t`def:ld-game` in\n    35\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-156`, with paper origin\n    36\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    37\t-/\n    38\tstructure LdParams where\n    39\t  q : ℕ\n    40\t  m : ℕ\n    41\t  d : ℕ\n    42\t  k : ℕ\n    43\t  hm : 1 ≤ m\n    44\t  hd : 1 ≤ d\n    45\t  hk : 1 ≤ k\n    46\t  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q\n    47\t  hdvd : m ∣ q\n    48\t\n    49\t/-- The positive dimension in `LdParams` supplies the finite coordinate type\n    50\tused by the uniform axis and prefix-index marginals. -/\n    51\tinstance (L : LdParams) : Nonempty (Fin L.m) :=\n    52\t  ⟨⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one L.hm⟩⟩\n    53\t\n    54\t/-- The fixed model accessor for an `LdParams` record.  It is a compatibility\n    55\tview of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently quantified\n    56\tparameter.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin\n    57\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    58\t-/\n    59\tnoncomputable def LdParams.model (P : LdParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=\n    60\t  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq\n    61\t\n    62\t/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed\n    63\tfield carrier in `def:ld-game`, selected globally by `LdParams.model`.\n    64\tBlueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin\n    65\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    66\t-/\n    67\tabbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := (P.model).K\n    68\t\n    69\t/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint\n    70\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`, paper origin\n    71\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    72\t-/\n    73\tinductive LdType where\n    74\t  | point\n    75\t  | aline\n    76\t  | dline\n    77\t  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype\n    78\t\n    79\t/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint\n    80\t`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; /-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,
this directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is
sampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.

This is the direct-index repair described in
`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second
definition of the source verifier game. -/
structure DirectLdParams where
  q : ℕ
  m : ℕ
  d : ℕ
  k : ℕ
  hm : 1 ≤ m
  hd : 1 ≤ d
  hk : 1 ≤ k
  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q

/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/
noncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=
  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq

/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/
abbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K

/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are
positive. -/
def DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=
  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩

instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩

/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its
field, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its
dimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.

The construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring
`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate
spaces used in the dimension-extension argument of
`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.
-/
def AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where
  q := P.q
  m := 2 * P.m + 2
  d := P.d
  k := 1
  hm := by omega
  hd := P.hd
  hk := by decide
  hq := P.hq

/-- A common random sample for the directly indexed question distribution.
The point, coordinate index, and unrestricted direction are mutually uniform. -/
structure DirectLdSpace (D : DirectLdParams) where
  point : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
  index : Fin D.m
  direction : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

instance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (DirectLdSpace D) :=
  ⟨⟨0, D.firstIndex, 0⟩⟩

/-- Removing the last coordinate and then applying `Parameters.next` recovers the
original non-base parameters. -/
theorem previous_next_eq (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
    (previous params hm).next = params := by
  cases params with
  | mk m q d hm0 hq hqPrimePower =>
      have hsub : m - 1 + 1 = m := Nat.sub_add_cancel (le_of_lt hm)
      simp [previous, Parameters.next, hsub]

/-- A bundled predecessor for a parameter set known to be a successor dimension. -/
structure SuccessorDecomposition (params : Parameters) where
  /-- The predecessor parameter bundle. -/
  pred : Parameters
  /-- The predecessor's successor is the original parameter bundle. -/
  next_eq : pred.next = params

/-- Every parameter bundle of dimension strictly larger than one has a bundled
predecessor whose successor is propositionally equal to the original bundle. -/
def successorDecompositionOfOneLtM (params : Parameters) (hm : 1 < params.m) :
    SuccessorDecomposition params where
  pred := previous params hm
  next_eq := previous_next_eq params hm

/-- A positive dimension that is not the base dimension is strictly larger than
one. -/
theorem one_lt_m_of_ne_one (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
    1 < params.m :=
  lt_of_le_of_ne params.hm (Ne.symm hm_ne_one)

/-- Non-base parameters have a bundled predecessor decomposition. -/
def successorDecompositionOfNeOne (params : Parameters) (hm_ne_one : params.m ≠ 1) :
    SuccessorDecomposition params :=
  successorDecompositionOfOneLtM params (one_lt_m_of_ne_one params hm_ne_one)

end Parameters

instance {params : Parameters} : NeZero params.q :=
  ⟨Nat.ne_of_gt params.hq⟩

abbrev Fq (params : Parameters) := Fin params.q
abbrev Point (params : Parameters) := Fin params.m → Fq params
abbrev PointTuple (params : Parameters) (k : ℕ) := Fin k → Fq params

instance {params : Parameters} : Inhabited (Fin params.m) :=
  ⟨⟨0, params.hm⟩⟩

instance {params : Parameters} : Inhabited (Fq params) :=
  ⟨⟨0, params.hq⟩⟩

/-- Prime-power metadata extracted from `params.hqPrimePower`, exposing the
honest finite-field carrier `GaloisField p n` underlying the paper's notation
`F_q`. -/
structure PrimePowerFieldSpec (params : Parameters) where
  p : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  pPrime : Nat.Prime p
  nPos : 0 < n
  cardEq : params.q = p ^ n

/-- Regard direct-game parameters as low individual degree test parameters.
The field size, dimension, and degree are unchanged. -/
@[reducible] def DirectLdParams.toLDTParameters (D : DirectLdParams) : Parameters where
  m := D.m
  q := D.q
  d := D.d
  hm := lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm
  hq := by
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := D.hq
    rw [hq]
    exact Nat.pow_pos (by decide)
  hqPrimePower := by
    obtain ⟨n, hn, hq⟩ := D.hq
    exact ⟨2, n, Nat.prime_two, hn.pos, hq⟩

/-- The fixed QPBT field model, viewed as the field model of the low
individual degree test. -/
@[reducible] noncomputable def DirectLdParams.toLDTFieldModel (D : DirectLdParams) :
    FieldModel D.toLDTParameters.q :=
  D.model.toFieldModel

/-- Coordinate coding from the direct scalar field to the LDT carrier. -/

    DirectScalarQ D ≃ Fq D.toLDTParameters :=

Second, the import of the classical\n    28\t  game's quantum soundness from the tensor-code paper carries two open\n    29\t  verification obligations at every dimension: the asserted identity with\n    30\t  the cited tensor-code test is not an identity and must be replaced by a\n    31\t  reduction with a value bound, and the source's instantiation of the\n    32\t  theorem's auxiliary parameter violates its lower bound at small\n    33\t  dimensions (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}).\n    34\t  \\item \\textbf{Estimated weight:} for the recommended direction, about\n    35\t  \\textbf{3--5 new definitions or interfaces} (a line-point distribution with\n    36\t  directly sampled index at arbitrary dimension, the directly indexed game,\n    37\t  and a restated soundness import) plus \\textbf{7--10 supporting lemmas},\n    38\t  including the strategy-transport layer between the directly indexed game\n    39\t  and the $\\chi$-based game (parsing pullback, seed-fiber averaging with\n    40\t  its open synchronicity-branch control, and a dilation--compression round\n    41\t  trip of the soundness conclusion); several hundred lines of formal proof.\n    42\t  Discharging the import obligations of\n    43\t  Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations} adds the pair-measurement\n    44\t  construction with its distributional matching, the branch-weight value\n    45\t  bound, and the parameter-bound case split.  The padding fallback is\n    46\t  heavier, roughly 6--10 reworked lemmas.\n    47\t  \\item \\textbf{Mathlib/project split:} approximately \\textbf{15\\% Mathlib}\n    48\t  and \\textbf{85\\% project-local}.  Mathlib supplies uniform distributions on\n    49\t  finite types and pushforward identities; the substance is choosing the\n    50\t  statement of the imported soundness theorem and rechecking the combining\n    51\t  subtree against it.\n    52\t  \\item \\textbf{Key Mathlib inputs:} uniform distributions on finite types\n    53\t  and their maps, and elementary divisibility arithmetic on powers of two.\n    54\t  The main inputs are project-local: the classical game, its conditionally\n    55\t  linear question distribution, and the imported soundness statement.\n    56\t  Tracked in \\localissue{0002}.\n    57\t\\end{itemize}\n    58\t\n    59\t\\section{Key theorem forms}\n    60\t\n    61\tThroughout, $q = 2^k$ with $k$ odd is an admissible field size, the tuple\n    62\t$(q,m,d)$ is admissible when moreover $d \\ge 1$ and $m \\mid q$, and\n    63\t$\\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$ denotes the $m$-variate polynomial representatives\n    64\tover $\\F_q$ of individual degree at most $d$.  The comparison involves four\n    65\ttheorem forms.\n    66\t\\begin{enumerate}\n    67\t  \\item \\textbf{Source theorem form} (the polynomial-pair measurement).  There\n    68\t  is a function $\\delta_S(\\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})$,\n    69\t  for universal constants $a > 1$ and $0 < b < 1$, such that for every\n    70\t  admissible $(q,m,d)$ and every projective strategy for the Pauli basis test\n    71\t  succeeding with probability at least $1-\\eps$, there is a projective\n    72\t  measurement $\\{\\hat S_{g_X,g_Z}\\}$ with outcomes pairs of polynomials in\n    73\t  $\\mathrm{ideg}_{d,m}(\\F_q)$ whose evaluations are $\\delta_S$-consistent, on\n    74\t  average over a uniform point $u \\in \\F_q^m$ and in both bases\n    75\t  $W \\in \\{X,Z\\}$, with the corresponding points measurements\n    76\t  $\\{\\hat M^{(\\mathrm{Point},W),u}_a\\}$ of the strategy, together with the\n    77\t  symmetric counterpart of this relation.\n    78\t  \\item \\textbf{Missing instantiation obligation.}  The classical low\n    79\t  individual degree game with parameter tuple $(q,\\, 2m+2,\\, d,\\, 1)$ is well\n    80\t  defined, and the combined point and line measurements assembled in the\n    81\t  analysis constitute a strategy for it of value at least\n    82\t  $1 - \\delta_{\\mathrm{combine}}$.  The game's question distribution draws\n    83\t  its axis and diagonal indices through an index function\n    84\t  $\\chi_{2m+2}\\colon \\F_q \\to \\{1,\\ldots,2m+2\\}$ with classes of equal size\n    85\t  $q/(2m+2)$, so the game exists only when $2m+2$ divides $q$.\n    86\t  \\item \\textbf{Restricted form supported by the present route.}  The source\n    87\t  theorem form under the additional hypothesis $2m+2 \\mid q$.  Among\n    88\t  admissible tuples this hypothesis holds exactly when $m = 1$ and\n    89\t  $q \\ge 8$; it fails for every admissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$ and for\n    90\t  $(q,m) = (2,1)$.\n    91\t  \\item \\textbf{Repaired import form} (recommended target).  Quantum\n    92\t  soundness of the directly indexed variant of the classical low individual\n    93\t  degree game over $\\F_q^{m'}$, for every dimension $m' \\ge 1$ and\n    94\t  admissible $q$, with no divisibility hypothesis: the question\n    95\t  distribution samples the axis index, and the diagonal prefix index,\n    96\t  uniformly from $\\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$ directly rather than through an index\n    97\t  function on $\\F_q$, and line questions carry the sampled index itself in\n    98\t  place of the seed $s \\in \\F_q$; the error is\n    99\t  $\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}(\\eps,q,m',d,k) = a(dm'k)^a(\\eps^b + q^{-b} +\n   100\t  2^{-bm'd})$.  This is a candidate target form, not an established one:\n   101\t  proving it carries the same two import obligations as the $\\chi$-based\n   102\t  import (Section~\\ref{sec:import-obligations}), and deriving the present\n   103\t  form from it when $m' \\mid q$ requires the strategy transport described\n   104\t  under the candidate repairs below, whose synchronicity step is an open\n   105\t  obligation.\n   106\t\\end{enumerate}\n   107\t\n   108\t\\section{The source assertion and the obstruction}\n   109\t\n   110\tWe examine the final step of the subsection ``Applying the classical\n   111\tlow-degree test'' in the analysis of the Pauli basis test in the compression\n   112\tpaper of Ji, Natarajan, Vidick, Wright, and Yuen (MIP$^{*}$=RE,\n   113\tarXiv:2001.04383), whose quantum soundness component builds on the low\n   114\tindividual degree test of \\cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree}.%\n   115\t\\footnote{Tracked in \\localissue{0002}.  In the mirror of the source\n   116\tconsulted here, the polynomial-pair lemma and its proof are at\n   117\t\\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},\n   118\tlines~1267--1288; the sub-line lemma is at lines~1063--1116 and the combined\n   119\tline lemma at lines~1020--1034 of the same file.  The game parametrization\n   120\twith its divisibility, the index function, the soundness statement with its\n   121\tproof, and admissibility are at\n   122\t\\path{references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex},\n   123\tlines~33--35, 214--219, 413--458, and 958--961.}\n   124\tThere, the combined point measurements\n   125\t$\\{\\hat Q^{x,z,\\alpha,\\beta}_c\\}$ and combined line measurements\n   126\t$\\{\\hat Q^{\\ell}_f\\}$, indexed by points of $\\F_q^{2m+2}$ and lines in\n   127\t$\\F_q^{2m+2}$, are asserted to form a strategy for the classical low\n   128\tindividual degree game with parameters\n   129\t\\[\n   130\t  \\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,\\, 2m+2,\\, d,\\, 1)\n   131\t  \\tag{\\path{lem:qld-4-7}}\n   132\t\\]\n   133\tof value $1 - \\delta_{\\mathrm{combine}}$, and the quantum soundness theorem\n   134\tfor that game is applied to produce the global polynomial-pair measurement.\n   135\tThe two lemmas feeding this step are stated for the line-point distribution\n   136\tover $\\F_q^{2m+2}$.\n   137\t\n   138\tThe game, however, is parametrized by tuples $(q,m',d,k)$ with $q$ an\n   139\tadmissible field size \\emph{and $m'$ dividing $q$}.  The divisibility is not\n   140\tincidental: the question distribution is a conditionally linear distribution\n   141\tin which a uniform seed coordinate $s \\in \\F_q$, read as an integer in\n   142\t$\\{0,\\ldots,q-1\\}$, determines the axis or diagonal index through the unique\n   143\t$\\chi(s)$ with\n   144\t\\[\n   145\t  s = (\\chi(s)-1)\\,\\frac{q}{m'} + r, \\qquad 0 \\le r < \\frac{q}{m'},\n   146\t  \\tag{\\path{eq:chi-func}}\n   147\t\\]\n   148\tso that the $m'$ classes $\\chi^{-1}(i)$ partition $\\F_q$ into sets of equal\n   149\tsize $q/m'$ and the index is uniform.  For $m' \\nmid q$ neither the index\n   150\tfunction nor the line-point distribution built from it is defined.\n   151\t\n   152\tAdmissibility of $(q,m,d)$ supplies only $m \\mid q$.  Since an admissible $q$\n   153\tis a power of two, $m \\mid q$ forces $m = 2^j$.  For $j \\ge 1$ the integer\n   154\t$m+1 \\ge 3$ is odd, so $2m+2 = 2(m+1)$ has an odd factor exceeding $1$ and\n   155\tdivides no power of two; for $m = 1$ the condition $4 \\mid q$ holds for every\n   156\tadmissible $q$ except $q = 2$.  Thus the instantiation at dimension $2m+2$ is\n   157\tundefined for every admissible tuple with $m \\ge 2$: for instance\n   158\t$(q,m,d) = (8,2,1)$ is admissible, while $6 \\nmid 8$.  The source performs\n   159\tthe instantiation without addressing the divisibility, so its proof route\n   160\testablishes the polynomial-pair lemma, and with it the soundness theorem for\n   161\tthe Pauli basis test that rests on it, only for $m = 1$ and $q \\ge 8$.\n   162\t\n   163\t\\section{What the cited soundness theorem requires: the import obligations}\n   164\t\\label{sec:import-obligations}\n   165\t\n   166\tThe quantum soundness theorem for the classical game inherits the constraint\n   167\t$m' \\mid q$ solely because it is stated for the game just described; its\n   168\tproof fixes an admissible $q$ with $m' \\mid q$, asserts that the game with\n   169\tsimultaneity parameter $1$ is \\emph{identical} to the two-prover tensor-code\n   170\ttest for the Reed--Solomon tensor code $\\mathcal C^{\\ot m'}$ of the same\n   171\tauthors' \\emph{Quantum soundness of testing tensor codes} (arXiv:2111.08131)\n   172\t\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}, and concludes by Theorem~4.7 there, instantiated with\n   173\tthat theorem's auxiliary integer parameter --- denoted $k$ in that source,\n   174\tand written $K$ here to avoid clashing with the field exponent and the\n   175\tsimultaneity parameter --- chosen as $(m')^3 d$.  Neither\n   176\tthe asserted identity nor the instantiation is complete as stated, so the\n   177\timport carries two verification obligations, which this section details and\n   178\twhich the blueprint's proof node for the soundness statement records as\n   179\topen.  Both obligations are independent of the divisibility question: they\n   180\tarise at every dimension, for the $\\chi$-based game where it is defined and\n   181\tequally for the directly indexed variant proposed under the candidate\n   182\trepairs.\n   183\t\n   184\t\\paragraph{The cited test.}\n   185\tIn the two-prover tensor-code test (Figures~1 and~2 of\n   186\t\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}; the two-prover strategy format and the goodness\n   187\tmeasure are Definitions~4.5 and~4.6 there), the referee performs one of\n   188\tthree subtests with probability $1/3$ each, assigning the two roles of each\n   189\tsubtest to the two provers uniformly at random.  \\emph{Axis-parallel lines\n   190\ttest}: sample a uniform point $u \\in [n]^{m'}$ and a uniform axis\n   191\t$j \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$; send the axis-parallel line $\\ell$ through $u$ in\n   192\tdirection $j$ to one prover, who answers a codeword $g \\in \\mathcal C$;\n   193\tsend $u$ to the other, who answers a field value $a$; accept iff\n   194\t$g(u_j) = a$.  \\emph{Subcube commutation test}: sample\n   195\t$j \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m'\\}$ and a subcube $H \\subseteq [n]^{m'}$ by fixing the\n   196\tlast $j-1$ coordinates uniformly; sample $u, v$ independently and uniformly\n   197\tin $H$ and a uniform order bit; send the ordered pair $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ to\n   198\tone prover, who answers a pair $(b_u, b_v)$ of field values; send $u$ to\n   199\tthe other, who answers $a$; accept iff $b_u = a$.  \\emph{Synchronicity\n   200\ttest}: send one identical question --- a line, a point, or an ordered\n   201\tpair, with probability $1/3$ each --- to both provers and accept iff their\n   202\tanswers agree.  Theorem~4.7 supposes a two-prover strategy passing this\n   203\ttest with probability $1-\\eps$ together with an integer parameter\n   204\t$K \\ge 12 m' t$, where $t$ is the interpolation parameter of the base code\n   205\t--- for the degree-$d$ Reed--Solomon code, of blocklength $n = q$ and\n   206\tdistance $q-d$, one has $t = d+1$ --- and produces projective measurements\n   207\t$\\{G_c\\}$ and $\\{\\tilde G_c\\}$ with outcomes in $\\mathcal C^{\\ot m'}$,\n   208\tconsistent with one prover's points measurements, with the other prover's\n   209\tlines measurements, and with each other, up to\n   210\t$\\eta'(m',t,K,\\eps,n^{-1}) = \\mathrm{poly}(m',t,K) \\cdot\n   211\t\\mathrm{poly}(\\eps, n^{-1}, e^{-K/(m')^2})$.\n   212\t\n   213\t\\paragraph{Obligation 1: the game correspondence.}\n   214\tThe source asserts that the $\\chi$-based game at parameters $(q,m',d,1)$\n   215\tis this test.  It is not, in four respects.\n   216\t(i)~The game has no pair questions.  A pair question of the test reveals\n   217\ttwo points of a \\emph{hidden} subcube --- the subcube itself is not sent\n   218\t--- and is answered by two field values, while the game's diagonal-line\n   219\tquestion reveals a full line description and is answered by a degree-$m'd$\n   220\tpolynomial.  A reduction must construct the pair measurements from the\n   221\tdiagonal-line measurements by post-processing (measure a line through $u$\n   222\tand $v$ and evaluate the answered polynomial at the two parameters), and\n   223\tboth directions of the information mismatch matter: the game's line\n   224\tdescription carries an index and a seed, neither of which is a function of\n   225\tthe pair $(u,v)$, so the constructed measurement must average over the\n   226\tcompatible indices and seeds; and the game's diagonal lines fix the\n   227\t\\emph{first} $i-1$ coordinates where the test's subcubes fix the\n   228\t\\emph{last} $j-1$, so the coordinate conventions must be aligned.  The\n   229\tconstruction must preserve projectivity and must match the law of the\n   230\thidden-subcube pair with the law induced by the game's diagonal sampling.\n   231\t(ii)~The game's line questions carry the seed $s \\in \\F_q$; the test's\n   232\tcarry only the line.  A strategy may depend on the seed beyond its class\n   233\t$\\chi^{-1}(i)$, and removing this dependence runs into the fiber-averaging\n   234\tdifficulty made explicit under the candidate repairs: averaging preserves\n   235\tthe line-versus-point branches exactly but not the synchronicity branches.\n   236\t(iii)~The branch weights differ: each nontrivial cross-test has mass $1/3$\n   237\tin the test against $2/9$ in the game.  Once the per-branch predicates are\n   238\tmatched, the intended bookkeeping bound is that the constructed strategy's\n   239\trejection probability in the test is at most $\\tfrac32$ times the game's\n   240\trejection probability, up to the $O(1/(m'q))$ of item~(iv); this bound is\n    25\topen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n    26\t\n    27\tnoncomputable section\n    28\t\n    29\t/-- Parameters for the directly indexed low-degree game.  Unlike `LdParams`,\n    30\tthis directly indexed line-space construction has no divisibility field: its coordinate index is\n    31\tsampled from `Fin m` rather than encoded by fibers of `chiIndex`.\n    32\t\n    33\tThis is the direct-index repair described in\n    34\t`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`; it is not a second\n    35\tdefinition of the source verifier game. -/\n    36\tstructure DirectLdParams where\n    37\t  q : ℕ\n    38\t  m : ℕ\n    39\t  d : ℕ\n    40\t  k : ℕ\n    41\t  hm : 1 ≤ m\n    42\t  hd : 1 ≤ d\n    43\t  hk : 1 ≤ k\n    44\t  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q\n    45\t\n    46\t/-- The canonical scalar model for directly indexed parameters. -/\n    47\tnoncomputable def DirectLdParams.model (D : DirectLdParams) : FixedFieldModel D.q :=\n    48\t  fixedFieldModel D.q D.hq\n    49\t\n    50\t/-- The scalar field of a directly indexed low-degree game. -/\n    51\tabbrev DirectScalarQ (D : DirectLdParams) := D.model.K\n    52\t\n    53\t/-- The first coordinate, available because directly indexed dimensions are\n    54\tpositive. -/\n    55\tdef DirectLdParams.firstIndex (D : DirectLdParams) : Fin D.m :=\n    56\t  ⟨0, lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one D.hm⟩\n    57\t\n    58\tinstance (D : DirectLdParams) : Nonempty (Fin D.m) := ⟨D.firstIndex⟩\n    59\t\n    60\t/-- The direct game used at the extended dimension of the combining map.  Its\n    61\tfield, degree, and simultaneity parameters are inherited from `P`, while its\n    62\tdimension is `2 * P.m + 2`; no divisibility assertion is introduced.\n    63\t\n    64\tThe construction has dimension `2 * P.m + 2` without requiring\n    65\t`2 * P.m + 2 ∣ P.q`; it supplies the directly indexed line and coordinate\n    66\tspaces used in the dimension-extension argument of\n    67\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:1257-1293`.\n    68\t-/\n    69\tdef AdmissibleParams.extendedDirectLd (P : AdmissibleParams) : DirectLdParams where\n    70\t  q := P.q\n    71\t  m := 2 * P.m + 2\n    72\t  d := P.d\n    73\t  k := 1\n    74\t  hm := by omega\n    75\t  hd := P.hd\n     1\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Combining.DirectLowDegree.Geometry\n     2\timport MIPStarRE.QPBT.Test.LowDegreeGameTheorems\n     3\t\n     4\t/-!\n     5\t# The directly indexed low-degree game\n     6\t\n     7\tThis module defines polynomial evaluation, questions, answers, and the game\n     8\tfor the directly indexed low-degree interface.\n     9\t\n    10\t## References\n    11\t\n    12\tThe underlying game is `def:ld-game` in\n    13\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with source origin\n    14\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n    15\t-/\n    16\t\n    17\topen scoped BigOperators\n    18\t\n    19\tnamespace MIPStarRE.QPBT\n    20\t\n    21\topen MIPStarRE.LDT\n    22\topen MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries\n    23\topen MIPStarRE.Quantum\n    24\t\n    25\tnoncomputable section\n    26\t\n    27\t/-- Coefficient lists for a univariate polynomial of degree at most `c` in the\n    28\tdirect scalar field. -/\n    29\tabbrev DirectDegPoly (D : DirectLdParams) (c : ℕ) :=\n    30\t  Fin (c + 1) → DirectScalarQ D\n    31\t\n    32\t/-- A direct line polynomial evaluates to `a` at `u` when `u` lies on the line\n    33\tand every parameter presenting `u` gives value `a`.  The universal clause\n    34\tkeeps the zero-direction case explicit. -/\n    35\tdef DirectEvaluatesTo {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ} (line : DirectLineDesc D)\n    36\t    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)\n    37\t    (a : DirectScalarQ D) : Prop :=\n    38\t  (∃ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction) ∧\n    39\t    ∀ t : DirectScalarQ D, u = line.base + t • line.direction →\n    40\t      evalCoefficient f t = a\n    41\t\n    42\t/-- Option-completed evaluation of a direct line polynomial.  `none` is an\n    43\texplicit outcome when the point does not determine an evaluation; no field\n    44\tvalue is used as a fallback. -/\n    45\tnoncomputable def directEvalOpt {D : DirectLdParams} {c : ℕ}\n    46\t    (line : DirectLineDesc D) (u : Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D)\n    47\t    (f : DirectDegPoly D c) : Option (DirectScalarQ D) := by\n    48\t  classical\n    49\t  exact if h : ∃ a : DirectScalarQ D, DirectEvaluatesTo line f u a then\n    50\t    some (Classical.choose h)\n    51\t  else none\n    52\t\n    53\t/-- The typed question alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/\n    54\tabbrev DirectLdQuestion (D : DirectLdParams) := LdType × DirectLdSpace D\n    55\t\n    56\t/-- Canonicalize a common direct sample for one question type.  Irrelevant\n    57\tcoordinates are fixed, so point questions reveal no sampled line index and\n    58\taxis-line questions reveal no diagonal direction. -/\n    59\tnoncomputable def directLdMap (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    60\t    LdType → DirectLdSpace D → DirectLdSpace D\n    61\t  | .point, sample => ⟨sample.point, D.firstIndex, 0⟩\n    62\t  | .aline, sample =>\n    63\t      let direction := coordinateDirection sample.index\n    64\t      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, 0⟩\n    65\t  | .dline, sample =>\n    66\t      let direction := directPrefixProjection sample.index sample.direction\n    67\t      ⟨lineRepMap direction sample.point, sample.index, direction⟩\n    68\t\n    69\t/-- The directly indexed question distribution.  It has the same uniform\n    70\tordered type-pair branches as `ldQuestionDistribution`, but its common sample\n    71\tcontains an actual coordinate index rather than a field seed. -/\n    72\tnoncomputable def directLdQuestionDistribution (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    73\t    Distribution (DirectLdQuestion D × DirectLdQuestion D) :=\n    74\t  (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map fun sample =>\n    75\t    ((sample.1.1, directLdMap D sample.1.1 sample.2),\n    76\t      (sample.1.2, directLdMap D sample.1.2 sample.2))\n    77\t\n    78\t/-- The directly indexed question law is probabilistic. -/\n    79\ttheorem directLdQuestionDistribution_isProbability (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    80\t    (directLdQuestionDistribution D).IsProbability := by\n    81\t  exact (uniformDistribution_isProbability\n    82\t    ((LdType × LdType) × DirectLdSpace D)).map _\n    83\t\n    84\t/-- The answer alphabet of the directly indexed game. -/\n    85\tinductive DirectLdAnswer (D : DirectLdParams) where\n    86\t  | pointVals (a : Fin D.k → DirectScalarQ D)\n    87\t  | alinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n    88\t  | dlinePolys (a : Fin D.k → Fin (D.m * D.d + 1) → DirectScalarQ D)\n    89\t  deriving DecidableEq\n    90\t\n    91\t/-- A finite code for the directly indexed answer alphabet. -/\n    92\tabbrev DirectLdAnswerCode (D In the simultaneous version, the players' answers are $k$-tuples, checked coordinatewise against a $k$-tuple of low individual degree polynomials.\n    16\t\n    17\t\\begin{definition}[The classical low individual degree game: parameters and registers]\\label{def:ld-game}\n    18\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldGame}\n    19\t\t\\leanok\n    20\t\t\\uses{def:game, def:admissible-size}\n    21\t\t% The source fixes \\N to be the set of positive integers\n    22\t\t% (references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:6) and takes m, d, ldc in \\N\n    23\t\t% (references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:33-35),\n    24\t\t% so the positivity below is the source's implicit domain, stated explicitly.\n    25\t\t% It is load-bearing: at d = 0 or k = 0 the prefactor a(dmk)^a of delta_ld in\n    26\t\t% lem:ld-soundness vanishes, and at d = 0 the resulting exact conclusions fail\n    27\t\t% (e.g. at (q,m,d,k) = (2,1,0,1) with eps = 1). The case k = 0, though it would\n    28\t\t% hold trivially, is likewise outside the source's domain and is omitted.\n    29\t\tThe game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is parametrized by a tuple $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$, where $m, d, k \\ge 1$ are integers, $q \\in \\N$ is an admissible field size (Definition~\\ref{def:admissible-size}), and $m$ divides $q$. We write $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ to emphasize the dependence on the parameter tuple. The type set of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is\n    30\t\t\\[\n    31\t\t\t\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} = \\{\\mathsf{Point}, \\mathsf{ALine}, \\mathsf{DLine}\\}\\;,\n    32\t\t\\]\n    33\t\tand the distribution over type pairs $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ is uniform over $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$. The ambient space is the direct sum $V = V_X \\oplus V_I \\oplus V_V$ of three register subspaces: the \\emph{point register} $V_X \\cong \\F_q^m$, the \\emph{coordinate register} $V_I \\cong \\F_q$, and the \\emph{direction register} $V_V \\cong \\F_q^m$. Elements of $V$ are identified with triples $(u,s,v) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q \\times \\F_q^m$. The question distribution and the win predicate of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ are specified in Definitions~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} and~\\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} below.\n    34\t\\end{definition}\n    35\t\n    36\t\\begin{definition}[Question distribution of the classical low individual degree game]\\label{def:ld-question-distribution}\n    37\t\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:cl-func, def:cl-dist, lem:cl-concat, def:cl-canonical, def:line-representative}\n    38\t\tLet $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ be as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}. Define $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$ to be the $1$-level CL function on $V$ that projects onto $V_X$: for every $(u,s,v) \\in V$,\n    39\t\t\\begin{equation}\n    40\t\t\t\\label{eq:cl-ptf}\n    41\t\t\tL_{\\mathsf{Point}}(u,s,v) = (u,0,0)\\;.\n    42\t\t\\end{equation}\n    43\t\tFor $s \\in \\F_q$, let $\\chi(s)$ be the unique integer such that\n    44\t\t\\begin{equation}\n    45\t\t\t\\label{eq:chi-func}\n    46\t\t\ts = (\\chi(s)-1)\\,\\frac{q}{m} + r\n    47\t\t\\end{equation}\n    48\t\tfor some $0 \\le r < q/m$, where $s$ is interpreted as an integer in $\\{0,1,\\ldots,q-1\\}$ under the identification of $\\F_q$ with binary strings fixed in Chapter~\\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra}. Since $m$ divides $q$, when $s$ is uniformly distributed on $\\F_q$ the index $\\chi(s)$ is uniformly distributed on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$. Define $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ by\n    49\t\t\\begin{equation}\n    50\t\t\t\\label{eq:cl-alnf}\n    51\t\t\tL_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v) = \\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\\, s,\\, 0\\bigr)\\quad\\text{for all } (u,s,v) \\in V\\;,\n    52\t\t\\end{equation}\n    53\t\twhere $i = \\chi(s)$ and $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_v$ denotes the canonical linear map with one-dimensional kernel spanned by $v$, used to compute canonical representatives of lines (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}). The function $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the concatenation (in the sense of Lemma~\\ref{lem:cl-concat}) of the $1$-level CL function projecting $V_I \\oplus V_V$ onto $V_I$ with the family of $1$-level CL functions $\\{L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}\\}$ on $V_X$ indexed by $i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,m\\}$; thus $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is a $2$-level CL function. Define $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ by\n    54\t\t\\begin{equation}\n    55\t\t\t\\label{eq:cl-dlnf}\n    56\t\t\tL_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v) = \\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{\\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\\, s,\\, \\pi_{i-1}(v)\\bigr)\\;,\n    57\t\t\\end{equation}\n    58\t\twhere $i = \\chi(s)$ and $\\pi_{i-1}$ zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of its input. The function $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the concatenation of (i) the identity on $V_I$, (ii) for each $i$ the $1$-level CL function $v \\mapsto \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ on $V_V$, and (iii) for each pair $(s,v') \\in V_I \\oplus V_V$ the $1$-level CL function $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ on $V_X$; thus $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is a $3$-level CL function.\n    59\t\n    60\t\tThe question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is the typed CL distribution obtained as follows: sample a type pair $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ uniformly from $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, sample $z = (u,s,v)$ uniformly from $V$, and send each player $w \\in \\{\\mathrm A,\\mathrm B\\}$ the question $(t_w, L_{t_w}(z))$.\n    61\t\\end{definition}\n    62\t\n    63\t\\begin{lemma}[Level of the axis-parallel line map]\\label{lem:ld-aline-level}\n    64\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinear_ldALineCL}\n    65\t\t\\leanok\n    66\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:cl-func}\n    67\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}. The map $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ of Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-alnf} is a $2$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.\n    68\t\\end{lemma}\n    69\t\\begin{proof}\n    70\t\t\\leanok\n    71\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative}\n    72\t\tThe following data exhibit $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ as a $2$-level conditionally linear function. Its first level is the projection of $V$ onto the coordinate register $V_I$, which is linear. For a first-level value with coordinate component $s$, its second level is the linear map $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}$ with $i = \\chi(s)$, acting on the point register $V_X$. The registers $V_I$ and $V_X$ are disjoint, so the second level is supported on a register subspace disjoint from the first, and summing the two contributions gives $\\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u),\\, s,\\, 0\\bigr)$, which is $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(u,s,v)$ by Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-alnf}.\n    73\t\\end{proof}\n    74\t\n    75\t\\begin{lemma}[Level of the diagonal line map]\\label{lem:ld-dline-level}\n    76\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.isCondLinear_ldDLineCL}\n    77\t\t\\leanok\n    78\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:cl-func}\n    79\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}. The map $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ of Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-dlnf} is a $3$-level conditionally linear function on $V$.\n    80\t\\end{lemma}\n    81\t\\begin{proof}\n    82\t\t\\leanok\n    83\t\t\\uses{def:cl-func, def:register-subspace, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative}\n    84\t\tThe following data exhibit $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ as a $3$-level conditionally linear function. Its first level is the projection of $V$ onto the coordinate register $V_I$. For a first-level value with coordinate component $s$, its second level is the linear map $v \\mapsto \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ with $i = \\chi(s)$ on the direction register $V_V$. For a second-level value with direction component $v'$, its third level is the linear map $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ on the point register $V_X$. The registers $V_I$, $V_V$ and $V_X$ are pairwise disjoint, so each level is supported on a register subspace disjoint from the preceding ones, and summing the three contributions gives $\\bigl(L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{\\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),\\, s,\\, \\pi_{i-1}(v)\\bigr)$, which is $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(u,s,v)$ by Equation~\\eqref{eq:cl-dlnf}.\n    85\t\\end{proof}\n    86\t\n    87\t\\begin{lemma}[The low-degree question distribution is a typed CL distribution]\\label{lem:ld-question-typed-cl}\n    88\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.ldQuestionDistribution_eq_typedCL}\n    89\t\t% No completion mark: the linked declaration proves the distribution identity only, not the typed-family assertion. See the last paragraph of the statement; the open family assertion is tracked by issue 180.\n    90\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:typed-cl-distributions, def:graph-distribution, lem:ld-aline-level, lem:ld-dline-level}\n    91\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game}, let $L = \\{L_t\\}_{t \\in \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}}$ be the family of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}, and let $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ be the graph on $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ all of whose unordered pairs, self-loops included, are edges. Then the question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ is the $(\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}, G^{\\mathrm{ld}})$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\\mu^{G^{\\mathrm{ld}}}_{L,\\,L}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions}. The linked declaration proves the distribution identity: the question distribution of $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}$ equals the distribution that the construction of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions} produces from the pair $(L, L)$ and the graph $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, a construction that is available for an arbitrary family of maps. It does not prove that $L$ is a $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$-typed family of conditionally linear functions of one common level, which is what makes the right-hand side a typed conditionally linear distribution in the sense of Definition~\\ref{def:typed-cl-distributions}: Lemmas~\\ref{lem:ld-aline-level} and~\\ref{lem:ld-dline-level} give the levels of $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ and $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$, while the level of $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$ and the passage of the three maps to a common level are not formalized. That family assertion is open and is tracked as issue~\\#180, so the statement and the proof below carry no completion mark.\n    92\t\\end{lemma}\n    93\t\\begin{proof}\n    94\t\t% No completion mark: the Lean proof establishes the distribution identity only; the typed-family hypotheses on L are open and tracked by issue 180.\n    95\t\t\\uses{def:typed-cl-distributions, def:graph-distribution, def:cl-dist}\n    96\t\tEvery unordered pair of types is an edge of $G^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, so the graph distribution $\\mu_{G^{\\mathrm{ld}}}$ of Definition~\\ref{def:graph-distribution} is the uniform distribution on $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}} \\times \\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$. For each ordered type pair $(t_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B})$ the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{t_{\\mathrm A}},\\, L_{t_{\\mathrm B}}}$ is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{t_{\\mathrm A}}(z), L_{t_{\\mathrm B}}(z)\\bigr)$. Binding the uniform type pair to these push-forwards and tagging each content with its type is exactly the two-stage sampling procedure of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}. This establishes the distribution identity; the typed-family hypotheses on $L$ are not established here.\n    97\t\\end{proof}\n    98\t\n    99\tThe next two lemmas show that the CL functions $L_{\\mathsf{Point}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, $L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ give rise to the axis-parallel and diagonal line-versus-point distributions.\n   100\tWe label the coordinates by $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,m-1\\}$, with label $r$\n   101\trepresenting the paper's coordinate $r+1$.\n   102\t\n   103\t\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:alnf}\n   104\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_mem_line}\n   105\t\t\\leanok\n   106\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n   107\t\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, e_i)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a line that goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n   108\t\\end{lemma}\n   109\t\\begin{proof}\n   110\t\t\\leanok\n   111\t\t\\uses{def:cl-dist, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative, lem:line-rep-incidence}\n   112\t\tBy Definition~\\ref{def:cl-dist} the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}(z), L_{\\mathsf{Point}}(z)\\bigr)$, so each marginal below is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on $V$ along the composite of that map with the corresponding coordinate. The point marginal is the image of the uniform distribution on $V$ under $(u,s,v) \\mapsto u$, hence uniform on $\\F_q^m$. The axis marginal is its image under $(u,s,v) \\mapsto \\chi(s)$; since $m$ divides $q$, every fibre of $\\chi$ has exactly $q/m$ elements, so $i = \\chi(s)$ is uniform on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$ and $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$. Finally the base point recorded in the sample is $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}(u)$, which is fixed by $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{e_i}$ (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}) and satisfies $u \\in \\ell(u_0,e_i)$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:line-rep-incidence}.\n   113\t\\end{proof}\n   114\t\n   115\t\\begin{lemma}\\label{lem:dlnf}\n   116\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_point_marginal_uniform, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_mem_line, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_prefix_zero}\n   117\t\t\\leanok\n   118\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:line}\n   119\t\tConsider the pair $(\\ell, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the tuple $\\bigl((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0)\\bigr)$ from the CL distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$, and let $\\ell = \\ell(u_0, v)$ where $i = \\chi(s)$. Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\\F_q^m$, and $\\ell$ is a random diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares its first $i-1$ coordinates with $u$, for uniformly random $i \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$.\n   120\t\\end{lemma}\n   121\t\\begin{proof}\n   122\t\t\\leanok\n   123\t\t\\uses{def:cl-dist, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line-representative, lem:line-rep-incidence}\n   124\t\tThe three steps are those of the proof of Lemma~\\ref{lem:alnf}, and none of them depends on that lemma. The two marginals are again push-forwards of the uniform distribution on $V$ along coordinates of $z \\mapsto \\bigl(L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}(z), L_{\\mathsf{Point}}(z)\\bigr)$, by Definition~\\ref{def:cl-dist}: the point marginal is uniform on $\\F_q^m$, and $i = \\chi(s)$ is uniform on $\\{1,2,\\ldots,m\\}$ because every fibre of $\\chi$ has $q/m$ elements. The direction component of the sampled tuple is $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$, whose first $i-1$ coordinates vanish and which is unchanged by a further application of $\\pi_{i-1}$. Finally $u_0 = L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}(u)$ is fixed by $L^{\\mathrm{Ln}}_{v'}$ (Definition~\\ref{def:line-representative}) and satisfies $u \\in \\ell(u_0,v')$ by Lemma~\\ref{lem:line-rep-incidence}.\n   125\t\\end{proof}\n   126\t\n   127\t\\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]\\label{def:line-point-dist}\n   128\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineKind, MIPStarRE.QPBT.LineDesc}\n   129\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist, MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist}\n   130\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist}\n   131\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.aLinePointDist_isProbability}\n   132\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.dLinePointDist_isProbability}\n   133\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_isProbability}\n   134\t\t\\leanok\n   135\t\t\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, lem:alnf, lem:dlnf}\n   136\t\tThe \\emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{ALine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,e_i),\\, u)$, where we omit the $0$ components for simplicity. The \\emph{diagonal line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$ is the distribution $\\mu_{L_{\\mathsf{DLine}}, L_{\\mathsf{Point}}}$ over pairs $(\\ell = (u_0,s,v),\\, u)$. The \\emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\\mathsf{Line}}$ is the equal mixture of the two: with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{ALine}}$, and with probability $\\tfrac12$ output a sample from $D_{\\mathsf{DLine}}$.\n   137\t\\end{definition}\n   138\t\n   139\t\\begin{definition}[Win predicate of the classical low individual degree game]\\label{def:ld-win-predicate}\n   140\t\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:line, def:polyfunc}\n   141\t\tFix $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$. Answers in the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ take the following forms, depending on the question type; answers not of the prescribed form are rejected.\n   142\t\t\\begin{itemize}\n   143\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{Point}$, question content $u \\in \\F_q^m$: the answer is an element of $\\F_q^k$.\n   144\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{ALine}$, question content $(u_0,s) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q$, specifying the axis-parallel line $\\ell(u_0,e_i)$ with $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple $(f_1,\\ldots,f_k)$ of univariate polynomials $f_j\\colon \\F_q \\to \\F_q$ of degree at most $d$, each given by its $d+1$ coefficients.\n   145\t\t\t\\item Type $\\mathsf{DLine}$, question content $(u_0,s,v) \\in \\F_q^m \\times \\F_q \\times \\F_q^m$, specifying the diagonal line $\\ell(u_0,v')$ with $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \\chi(s)$: the answer is a $k$-tuple of univariate polynomials of degree at most $md$.\n   146\t\t\\end{itemize}\n   147\t\tThe win predicate $D^{\\mathrm{ld}} = D^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the function of the tuple $(t_{\\mathrm A}, x_{\\mathrm A}, t_{\\mathrm B}, x_{\\mathrm B}, a_{\\mathrm A}, a_{\\mathrm B})$ determined by the following clauses, evaluated for $w \\in \\{\\mathrm A,\\mathrm B\\}$; in all cases where no action is indicated, the predicate accepts.\n   148\t\t\\begin{enumerate}\n   149\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Consistency test}) If $t_{\\mathrm A} = t_{\\mathrm B}$, accept if and only if $a_{\\mathrm A} = a_{\\mathrm B}$.\n   150\t\t\t% The source phrases both clauses with \"the\" t such that x = u_0 + tv; that phrase\n   151\t\t\t% does not determine t on diagonal questions with direction v' = 0, which the\n   152\t\t\t% question distribution samples with positive probability. The universal\n   153\t\t\t% quantification over t used here is the local correction; see the remark below.\n   154\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Axis-parallel line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \\mathsf{ALine}$ and $t_{\\overline w} = \\mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\\overline w})_j$ for all $j \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,k\\}$ and all $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t e_i$, where $i = \\chi(s)$.\n   155\t\t\t\\item (\\textbf{Diagonal line-versus-point test}) If $t_w = \\mathsf{DLine}$ and $t_{\\overline w} = \\mathsf{Point}$, accept if and only if $f_j(t) = (a_{\\overline w})_j$ for all $j \\in \\{1,2,\\ldots,k\\}$ and all $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$, where $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v)$ and $i = \\chi(s)$.\n   156\t\t\\end{enumerate}\n   157\t\tThe game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$ is the typed game with type set $\\mathcal T^{\\mathrm{ld}}$, the question distribution of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}, and win predicate $D^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$.\n   158\t\\end{definition}\n   159\t\n   160\t\\begin{remark}[Diagonal questions with zero direction]\\label{rem:ld-win-zero-direction}\n   161\t\tThe source states the two line-versus-point clauses with ``the'' $t \\in \\F_q$ such that $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v$. When the direction is nonzero and $x_{\\overline w}$ lies on the line, exactly one such $t$ exists and the formulation above agrees with the source. But zero directions occur: Definition~\\ref{def:line} explicitly permits them, and the question distribution of Definition~\\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} produces $\\mathsf{DLine}$ questions with $v' = \\pi_{i-1}(v) = 0$ with positive probability, namely whenever the last $m - i + 1$ coordinates of $v$ vanish. In that case $\\ell(u_0, 0) = \\{u_0\\}$, every $t \\in \\F_q$ satisfies $x_{\\overline w} = u_0 + t v'$ when $x_{\\overline w} = u_0$, and the source clause does not determine acceptance for a nonconstant answer polynomial. The universal quantification over $t$ adopted in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-win-predicate} makes the predicate a well-defined function of its arguments; it accepts vacuously when no such $t$ exists, a case the question distribution never produces. Completeness is unaffected: the restriction of a polynomial $g$ to the singleton line $\\ell(u_0,0)$, expressed through the parameterization $t \\mapsto u_0 + t \\cdot 0$, is the constant polynomial with value $g(u_0)$, which passes the check for every $t$. Soundness is likewise unaffected: zero directions occur with probability at most $2/(mq)$, so any acceptance convention on this event changes success probabilities by at most that amount; the game-correspondence obligation enumerated in the proof of Theorem~\\ref{lem:ld-soundness} accounts for this event explicitly, and an error of this shape is absorbed into the universal constants of $\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}$.\n   162\t\\end{remark}\n   163\t\n   164\tThe soundness properties of the low individual degree game are expressed in terms of the following class of measurements.\n   165\t\n   166\t\\begin{definition}[Low-degree polynomial measurements]\\label{def:ld-meas}\n   167\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyIndex, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeas, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeasFamily, MIPStarRE.QPBT.PolyMeasTuple}\n   168\t\t\\leanok\n   169\t\t\\uses{def:polyfunc, def:polymeasurements, def:polynomials-degree}\n   170\t\tLet $\\polymeas{m}{q}{d}$ denote the set of POVM measurements indexed by $\\polyfunc{m}{q}{d}$, the polynomial representatives of individual degree at most $d$ in each variable; this is the notion of Definition~\\ref{def:polymeasurements}, and the argument order $(m,q,d)$ follows that definition (the paper orders the arguments as $(m,d,q)$). By Definition~\\ref{def:polynomials-degree}, evaluation identifies these representatives with the corresponding polynomial functions $g\\colon \\F_q^m \\to \\F_q$, bijectively whenever $d \\le q-1$; at the canonical parameters (Definition~\\ref{def:introparams}, where $d = 1 \\le q-1$) the identification is bijective; the general statements of this chapter quantify over all admissible tuples and are read through the representative convention. More generally, for an integer $k$ and tuples $m = (m_1,\\ldots,m_k)$, $q = (q_1,\\ldots,q_k)$, $d = (d_1,\\ldots,d_k)$, let $\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)$ denote the set of measurements $G = \\{G_{g_1,\\ldots,g_k}\\}$ such that for each $i \\in \\{1,\\ldots,k\\}$, the outcome index $g_i$ is a polynomial $g_i\\colon \\F_{q_i}^{m_i} \\to \\F_{q_i}$ of individual degree at most $d_i$.\n   171\t\tThe tuple components are labelled by $r\\in\\{0,\\ldots,k-1\\}$, with\n   172\t\tlabel $r$ representing the paper's component $r+1$.\n   173\t\\end{definition}\n   174\t\n   175\tQuantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \\emph{total} degree was claimed by Natarajan and Vidick, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test by Vidick; there is a known gap in the soundness analysis of that test, and it is not used here. Instead, the construction relies on the low \\emph{individual} degree test, whose quantum soundness is proved in~\\cite{Ji2020LowIndividualDegree} and generalized in~\\cite{Ji2021Quantum}. The statement below is the form most directly useful in what follows.\n   176\t\n   177\t% The paper states this result in a theorem environment with the label lem:ld-soundness.\n   178\t% We keep both the environment and the label verbatim for cross-reference fidelity.\n   179\t\\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test]\\label{lem:ld-soundness}\n   180\t\t\\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.deltaLd, MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness}\n   181\t\t\\leanok\n   182\t\t\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:projective-strategy-general, def:tensor-product-value, def:consistency, def:bracket}\n   183\t\tThere exists a function\n   184\t\t\\[\n   185\t\t\t\\delta_{\\mathrm{ld}}(\\eps, q, m, d, k) = a\\,(dmk)^a \\bigl(\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\\bigr)\n   186\t\t\\]\n   187\t\tfor universal constants $a \\ge 1$ and $0 < b \\le 1$ such that the following holds. For all $\\eps > 0$ and every parameter tuple $\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\ref{def:ld-game} (so $m, d, k \\ge 1$, $q$ is an admissible field size, and $m$ divides $q$), and for all projective strategies $(\\psi, A, B)$ that succeed with probability at least $1-\\eps$ in the game $\\mathfrak{G}^{\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\mathsf{ldparams}}$, there exist measurements\n   188\t\t\\[\n   189\t\t\tG^w \\in \\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)\n   190\t\t\\]\n    30\t\n    31\t/-- Numerical parameters for the low-degree game.  The ambient coefficient\n    32\tspace uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq`, rather than a\n    33\tmodel supplied by each parameter record. This\n   110\tis `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint\n   111\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin\n   112\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.\n   113\t-/\n   114\tnoncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by\n   115\t  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by\n   116\t    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩\n   117\t  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))\n   118\t\n   119\t/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the\n   120\tchosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector. This is the `L_DLine` clause of\n   155\t`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint\n   156\t`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin\n   157\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).\n   158\t-/\n   159\tnoncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=\n   160\t  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)\n   161\t  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)\n   162\t  let rep := lineRepMap direction\n   163\t  fun i => match i with\n   164\t  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j\n   165\t  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))\n   166\t  | .inr j => direction j\n   167\t\n   168\t/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type. This is the direct-index analogue of `lem:dlnf`, paper\n`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:261-272`,\nand is a named obligation in the dimension-divisibility repair. -/\ntheorem directDLinePointDist_point_index_marginal_uniform (D : DirectLdParams) :\n    (directDLinePointDist D).map Prod.snd =\n        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) ∧\n      (directDLinePointDist D).map (fun sample => sample.1.index) =\n        uniformDistribution (Fin D.m) := by\n  constructor\n  · unfold directDLinePointDist\n    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability\n      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))\n      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]\n    simpa [Function.comp_def] using\n      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv\n        (e := directLdSpacePointEquiv D)\n        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.point) (by intro; rfl))\n  · unfold directDLinePointDist\n    rw [distribution_map_map_of_isProbability\n      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D))\n      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (DirectLdSpace D))]\n    simpa [Function.comp_def, directDLineDescOf, DirectLineDesc.index] using\n      (uniformDistribution_map_fst_of_equiv\n        (e := directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D)\n        (f := fun sample : DirectLdSpace D => sample.index) (by intro; rfl))\n\n/-- Every sampled direct diagonal line contains its paired point. 11\t## References\n    12\t\n    13\tThe line-point distributions originate in\n    14\t`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-272`.\n    15\tThe directly indexed
